label: copy-phase input w
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, at steps where the fed-back input token is w (i.e. the model just emitted w and it is now its input). Never fires on w in the original phase, on <DEL>, or on any other token; 100% of activations are copy-phase w inputs. About 19% of copy-phase w inputs are inactive, mostly early steps in short sequences (t<=6); activation is weak at early t and small L and grows with t/sequence length. Strongest activations are on w originally placed late in a long sequence, often repeated w (ww), and the first w of a repeated pair tends to be higher than the second.

issues: The core claims hold. All activation is in the copy phase on w inputs (test recall 1.0, mass recall 1.0, 0 missed activations). There is no activation in the original phase or on <DEL>, and none on any other token. Every active step has in_first==0, which follows from the copy phase. Precision is 0.813 on test.

One factual claim is wrong: the inactive w inputs are not 'mostly early steps (t <= 6)'. On test, the predicate restricted to t<=6 gives 8470 predicted at precision 0.416, about 4.9k false positives. Restricted to t>=7 it gives 82516 predicted at precision 0.853, about 12.1k false positives. So about 71% of the 17045 false positives are at t>=7. Even at late steps, roughly 15% of copy-phase w inputs stay inactive.

The late false positives look diffuse rather than systematic. Precision sits at about 0.85-0.91 across out_tok letter/digit, in_count, n_digits, prev_tok digit and recall_idx>=2. This looks like threshold noise on a graded magnitude.

There are mild lower-precision pockets. When the w was the first original token (recall_idx==1), precision is 0.64. On the final copy step (to_go==0), it is 0.68. When t<=6, it is 0.42. These match the weak-at-small-t/L account but are not a separate counterexample class.

The claim that 'the first w of a pair activates more strongly than the second' is only anecdotal. A w that follows a w (prev_tok==w) still fires at precision 0.91. When the next output is also w (out_tok==w), precision is 0.97. Both members of a doubled w reliably fire.
The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
